newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds finished higher but underperformed Bunds and eased from the day's highs as sellers held sway.
"It's been a mixed performance although we traded up a bit today," said one dealer.
But he said domestic sellers contributed to the narrowing of the 10-year Dutch/German yield spread to four basis points from six basis points the previous day.
The dealer said he saw selling of 10 and 15 year paper and switching into shorter maturities. "We have seen steady buying of the mid curve, especially 2000s," he said.
Shorter guilder paper had been been underperforming longer bonds in recent times on speculation of an interest rate hike.
Dealers said some investors switching back in Dutch bonds from German Bunds when the spread hit five basis points.
"But there was clearly not enough demand there to support them," said a trader.
Another trader said although prices finished higher, they were "very well offered" amid talk of a big seller.
He said that with Dutch yields nearing three-year lows, no buyers could be found, adding that a Dfl 250 million 11-year Eurobond from Nederlandsche Waterschapsbank had no impact.
"It's very expensive. We don't see any buyers," he said.
The bond was issued at an 18 basis point spread to the interpolated government bond yield.
